headline_summary: NVIDIA's new Vera Rubin NVL72 benchmark sets a performance baseline for inference while regulators in the US and China tighten AI governance, and open‑source tools expand options for local LLM deployment.

stories.title: NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 tops MLPerf Inference v6.1 benchmarks
stories.summary: NVIDIA's Vera Rubin NVL72 system achieved leading scores across multiple inference workloads in the MLPerf v6.1 suite, including large language model serving. The results emphasize gains in raw performance, scaling efficiency, and continuous optimization, targeting the high cost of token generation for enterprises.
stories.why_it_matters: Faster, more efficient inference reduces operational costs for large‑scale AI deployments.

stories.title: 2026 AI compliance guide outlines inventory, risk classification, vendor review
stories.summary: A recent blog post provides a step‑by‑step framework for businesses to meet 2026 AI regulations, recommending creation of an AI inventory, risk‑based classification, vendor security assessments, usage policies, and governance ownership. The guidance reflects tightening legal expectations across data privacy, security, and model oversight.
stories.why_it_matters: Companies can align their AI deployments with emerging regulatory requirements and avoid penalties.

stories.title: China releases AI safety governance playbook with risk grading standards
stories.summary: Chinese authorities published a safety governance framework that defines national standards for classifying and grading AI security risks and mandates industry‑specific rules for risk assessment and mitigation. The document outlines procedures for scenario‑based grading and sector‑tailored guidelines.
stories.why_it_matters: The standards set a benchmark for AI risk management that may influence global safety practices.

stories.title: GitHub curates open‑source inference engines and lightweight LLM runtimes
stories.summary: A GitHub repository lists several open‑source projects that enable local or high‑throughput LLM serving, including LocalAI, KoboldCPP, llamafile, vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT‑LLM, ExLlamaV3, Aphrodite Engine, TabbyAPI, and LlamaEdge. These tools provide drop‑in OpenAI‑compatible APIs, single‑file executables, or GPU‑optimized inference engines.
stories.why_it_matters: Developers can deploy LLMs without relying on proprietary cloud APIs, reducing latency and cost.
